display.purpose: Project statements, major section headings, and work-card titles.

body.purpose: Strategy narrative, service lists, subtitles, and supporting information.

label.purpose: Compact uppercase labels that anchor editorial rows.

motion.name: header-surface
motion.purpose: Moves the fixed header from transparent over the client hero to the dark Oglas navigation surface.

motion.name: reveal-progressive
motion.value: intersection-triggered with a 2000ms visibility safety net
motion.purpose: Enhances case-study pacing without ever making content depend on motion for visibility.

components.name: Case Metadata Chip
components.description: Compact project and year facts placed inside the opening brand statement.
components.css: .ds-case-meta { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; border: 1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / 0.6); border-radius: 9999px; padding: 4px 16px; color: #fff; background: transparent; font-family: Manrope, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.5; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Detail Row
components.description: The reusable label-and-content structure for overview, services, brand design, and identity chapters.
components.html:
OVERVIEW

A concise strategic explanation supports the visual story.
components.css: .ds-detail-row { display: grid; gap: 24px; color: #000; } .ds-detail-label { margin: 0; font-family: Manrope, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.01em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-detail-copy { margin: 0; max-width: 1100px; font-family: Manrope, sans-serif; font-size: clamp(16px, 1.35vw, 22px); line-height: 1.55; } @media (min-width: 1024px) { .ds-detail-row { grid-template-columns: 0.28fr 1fr; gap: 64px; } }

components.name: Service List
components.description: A quiet, hairline-divided inventory of project services inside a detail row.
components.css: .ds-service-list { margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; color: #000; font-family: Manrope, sans-serif; font-size: clamp(20px, 2vw, 32px); } .ds-service-list li { border-bottom: 1px solid rgb(0 0 0 / 0.15); padding: 20px 0; }

components.name: Image Board
components.description: A square-cornered, ratio-preserving frame for supplied brand-book artwork.
components.html: BRAND APPLICATION
components.css: .ds-image-board { display: grid; aspect-ratio: 1920 / 995; place-items: center; overflow: hidden; background: var(--bg-dark, #0c0c0c); color: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.55); border-radius: 0; font-family: Manrope, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Work Card
components.description: The shared portfolio handoff used in the final More work section.
components.html:
2025•VELVET PROPERTIES

The art of realty.
components.css: .ds-work-card { display: block; color: inherit; text-decoration: none; outline-offset: 8px; } .ds-work-card:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #e3ff51); } .ds-work-frame { aspect-ratio: 920 / 582; overflow: hidden; background: var(--bg-dark, #0c0c0c); } .ds-work-title { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 12px; margin-top: 20px; font-family: 'Vend Sans', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif; font-size: clamp(20px, 1.77vw, 34px); line-height: 1.02; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.02em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-work-title span { opacity: 0.6; } .ds-work-card p { margin: 12px 0 0; font-family: Manrope, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; opacity: 0.6; }

components.name: Primary Navigation Link
components.description: The Oglas header link treatment shared above every client-specific opening statement.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { position: relative; display: block; padding: 12px 0; color: #fff; font-family: Manrope, sans-serif; font-size: 14.72px; line-height: 1.5; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; transition: color 200ms; } .ds-nav-link::after { content: ''; position: absolute; right: 0; bottom: 4px; left: 0; height: 1px; background: currentColor; transform: scaleX(0); transform-origin: left; transition: transform 200ms; } .ds-nav-link:hover, .ds-nav-link[aria-current="page"] { color: var(--accent, #e3ff51); } .ds-nav-link:hover::after, .ds-nav-link[aria-current="page"]::after { transform: scaleX(1); } .ds-nav-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #e3ff51); outline-offset: 5px; }

narrative.overview:
An Oglas case study should feel less like a portfolio template and more like stepping inside a finished identity. The shared interface is editorial, quiet, and structurally consistent; it establishes pacing, legibility, and navigation, then recedes so the client work can lead. Each project opens with a bespoke, full-scale brand statement before moving through context, identity, applications, and a final invitation to explore more work.

The system deliberately separates the Oglas frame from the client's visual world. Oglas owns the page shell, typography for explanatory copy, information hierarchy, image-board rhythm, global navigation, work cards, and footer. The client owns the hero palette, marks, campaign language, brand imagery, and any project-specific bands. Velvet's deep green and copper geometry, Fishwala's navy identity, and Gymkha's monochrome athletic world are scoped expressions, not additions to the global Oglas token set.
keyCharacteristics: Image-led storytelling with full-width brand-book boards.
A restrained black, white, and lime Oglas frame around client-specific worlds.
Large condensed display type paired with clear, compact body copy.
Alternation between immersive visual sequences and concise editorial explanation.
One responsive structure that remains complete from mobile through wide desktop.

rules.name: The Client World Boundary Rule
rules.body: A client's palette may transform its hero, boards, and project-specific bands, but it never becomes a global Oglas token. In particular, Gymkha's black-and-white system is a scoped brand expression, not a site-wide palette decision.

rules.name: The Lime Means Interface Rule
rules.body: Keep signal lime attached to navigation, focus, and interactive state. Do not recolor client artwork or case-study narrative with it unless lime belongs to that client's supplied identity.

rules.name: The Artwork Keeps Its Voice Rule
rules.body: Do not imitate a client's proprietary typeface across Oglas UI. Use Oglas display and body roles for live interface text; preserve client typography inside supplied boards or a deliberately scoped hero treatment.

rules.name: The Short Copy Rule
rules.body: Narrative blocks explain strategy only where they strengthen the visual story. Keep them compact enough that the next application board remains the dominant reading reward.

rules.name: The Shared Spine Rule
rules.body: Preserve the sequence of bespoke opening statement, first application board, editorial context, identity/application rhythm, and “More work” handoff even when the number and grouping of boards differ.

rules.name: The Board Leads Rule
rules.body: Explanatory text is a pause between visual chapters, not a competing poster. Give the largest share of page area to high-fidelity project imagery.

rules.name: The Flat Gallery Rule
rules.body: Do not add decorative drop shadows to boards, narrative rows, service lists, or work cards. Depth comes from sequencing and tonal transitions.

dos: Do preserve the wide shared shell, editorial detail row, board rhythm, “More work” handoff, global navigation, and footer across every case study.
Do let each supplied brand book determine its project's palette, marks, campaign language, board ratios, and visual density.
Do use concise live text and descriptive alternative text to make the visual story understandable and accessible.
Do keep interaction states unmistakably Oglas, including visible keyboard focus and motion fallbacks for reduced-motion users.
donts: Don't promote a client-specific color, type treatment, mark, or slogan into the global Oglas token system.
Don't make Gymkha's black-and-white palette the default for other case studies; it belongs to Gymkha's scoped visual world.
Don't flatten Velvet, Fishwala, Gymkha, or future clients into one generic hero composition.
Don't add decorative cards, shadows, gradients, or interface chrome between boards when spacing and tonal contrast already establish the chapter break.
Don't omit narrative, application boards, or “More work” on mobile; adapt the grid and spacing instead.
